::: {#exm-biased-variance-mle}
#### A biased estimator of the variance

Let $\dsn{X}$ be mutually independent,
each with expectation $\mean$ and variance $\varpar$,
and let $n \ge 2$.
Consider two estimators of $\varpar$:

- the [sample variance](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-variance)
  $S^2 \eqdef \frac{1}{n-1} \sumin (\Rvar_\iobs - \bar X)^2$;
- the divide-by-$n$ estimator
  $\hvarpar \eqdef \avgin (\Rvar_\iobs - \bar X)^2$.

Both estimators are built from the sum of squared deviations
$\sumin (\Rvar_\iobs - \bar X)^2$,
so we first find its expectation.
Using

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \E{\Rvar_\iobs^2} &= \Var{\Rvar_\iobs} + \sqf{\E{\Rvar_\iobs}} \\
  &= \varpar + \mean^2
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \E{\bar X^2} &= \Var{\bar X} + \sqf{\E{\bar X}} \\
  &= \varpar/n + \mean^2
\end{aligned}
$$

(by @exm-mse-sample-mean and @exm-bias-sample-mean):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{\sumin (\Rvar_\iobs - \bar X)^2}
&= \E{\sumin \paren{\Rvar_\iobs^2 - 2 \Rvar_\iobs \bar X + \bar X^2}}
&& \text{(expand each square)}\\
&= \E{\sumin \Rvar_\iobs^2 - \sumin 2 \Rvar_\iobs \bar X + \sumin \bar X^2}
&& \text{(distribute the sum over the terms)}\\
&= \E{\sumin \Rvar_\iobs^2 - 2\bar X \sumin \Rvar_\iobs + \sumin \bar X^2}
&& \text{(factor $2\bar X$ out of the middle sum)}\\
&= \E{\sumin \Rvar_\iobs^2 - 2\bar X \sumin \Rvar_\iobs + n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\bar X^2$)}\\
&= \E{\sumin \Rvar_\iobs^2 - 2\bar X \cdot n \bar X + n \bar X^2}
&& \text{($\textstyle\sumin \Rvar_\iobs = n \bar X$)}\\
&= \E{\sumin \Rvar_\iobs^2 - 2n \bar X^2 + n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(multiply $2\bar X \cdot n \bar X$)}\\
&= \E{\sumin \Rvar_\iobs^2 - n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(collect the $\bar X^2$ terms)}\\
&= \E{\sumin \Rvar_\iobs^2} - \E{n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}\\
&= \sumin \E{\Rvar_\iobs^2} - \E{n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}\\
&= \sumin \E{\Rvar_\iobs^2} - n \E{\bar X^2}
&& \text{(factor the constant $n$ out of the expectation)}\\
&= \sumin (\varpar + \mean^2) - n \E{\bar X^2}
&& \text{(substitute $\E{\Rvar_\iobs^2}$)}\\
&= n(\varpar + \mean^2) - n \E{\bar X^2}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\varpar + \mean^2$)}\\
&= n(\varpar + \mean^2) - n\paren{\frac{\varpar}{n} + \mean^2}
&& \text{(substitute $\E{\bar X^2}$)}\\
&= n\varpar + n\mean^2 - n\paren{\frac{\varpar}{n} + \mean^2}
&& \text{(distribute $n$ over $\varpar + \mean^2$)}\\
&= n\varpar + n\mean^2 - \paren{n \cdot \frac{\varpar}{n} + n\mean^2}
&& \text{(distribute $n$ over $\frac{\varpar}{n} + \mean^2$)}\\
&= n\varpar + n\mean^2 - \paren{\varpar + n\mean^2}
&& \text{(cancel $n$ in $n \cdot \frac{\varpar}{n}$)}\\
&= n\varpar + n\mean^2 - \varpar - n\mean^2
&& \text{(distribute the minus sign)}\\
&= n\varpar - \varpar
&& \text{(cancel $n\mean^2$)}\\
&= (n - 1)\varpar
&& \text{(factor out $\varpar$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \E{S^2} &= \frac{1}{n-1}(n-1)\varpar \\
  &= \varpar,
\end{aligned}
$$

and by @thm-bias-exprs,
$\bias{S^2} = 0$:
the sample variance is [unbiased](#def-unbiased).

For the divide-by-$n$ estimator,
$\E{\hvarpar} = \frac{1}{n}(n-1)\varpar$, so:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bias{\hvarpar}
&= \E{\hvarpar} - \varpar
&& \text{(bias equals expectation minus truth)}\\
&= \frac{n-1}{n}\varpar - \varpar
&& \text{(substitute $\E{\hvarpar}$)}\\
&= \frac{n-1}{n}\varpar - \frac{n}{n}\varpar
&& \text{(write $\varpar$ over the common denominator $n$)}\\
&= \frac{n - 1 - n}{n}\varpar
&& \text{(combine the fractions)}\\
&= \frac{-1}{n}\varpar
&& \text{($n - 1 - n = -1$)}\\
&= -\frac{\varpar}{n}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\end{aligned}
$$

This estimator is biased:
on average it underestimates $\varpar$,
by an amount that shrinks to zero as $n$ grows.
:::
